purpose: Dornase alfa is used to help people with cystic fibrosis breathe more easily. It works by thinning and loosening the thick, sticky mucus that builds up in the lungs. This makes it easier to cough up the mucus and helps prevent lung infections.
how_it_works: Inside your lungs, thick mucus builds up partly because of DNA released from dead cells during infections. Dornase alfa is a man-made enzyme that breaks down that DNA, making the mucus much thinner and less sticky. Once the mucus is thinner, your lungs can clear it out more easily when you cough.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include a sore throat or hoarse voice, a runny nose, chest pain or discomfort, a skin rash, and eye redness or irritation. Some people also notice a change in their voice after using it.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding before using this medication. Let your healthcare team know about all other medications you are taking. Always use dornase alfa with the specific nebulizer recommended by your doctor, as other devices may not work properly. Do not mix it with other medications in the nebulizer cup.
typical_dosing: The usual dose for most patients is 2.5 mg (one ampule) inhaled through a nebulizer once a day. Some patients may use it twice a day based on their doctor's recommendation. It is best to use it at the same time each day to keep it working consistently.
